introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: Oh! Beef Noodle Soup ("we", "our", or "us") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website, use our mobile application, or dine at our restaurants.

infoCollect.title: Information We Collect

personalData.title: Personal Data You Provide
items: Name, email address, and phone number
Payment information (processed securely by our payment provider)

howWeUse.title: How We Use Your Information
items: Communicate with you about orders and promotions

children.title: Children's Privacy

body.thesis: Oh! serves premium American beef noodle soup in {pods} private dining pods inside {sqft} square feet. Guests order at a kiosk, the kitchen delivers through a hatch in each pod, and no host, server, or tip ever enters the room. That one design choice moves labor and seating economics away from casual dining and toward the best of fast casual.
body.unit: Open {days} days a year and serving about {covers} guests a day at a {check} average check, the unit produces {revenue} in revenue. Food runs {food} with American Wagyu and USDA Prime costed bowl by bowl, labor {labor}, and four-wall EBITDA {ebitda}. We ask investors to hold us to {target}, with {stretch} as the stretch at maturity. Break-even is about {breakEven} guests a day, and a {capex} build pays back in {payback} from opening.
body.growth: By year five the plan runs {corporate} company restaurants and {franchise} franchised ones, on a phased franchise schedule that respects the time a franchise disclosure document takes to become effective. Company revenue reaches {y5Revenue}. Corporate overhead of {overhead} sits inside that figure, leaving consolidated EBITDA of {consolidated}.
body.ask: The plan raises {capital} in two rounds with no debt. {cashLine} A financial partner takes preferred equity with a {pref} preferred return and a {liq} liquidation preference, and the common stake is derived from the return math and capped at {partner}. At that cap the partner's multiple is {multiple5} at a year-five exit and {multiple7} at a year-seven exit on the hybrid multiple. We state this plainly instead of asserting a split.
body.risks: The downside case is shown in full, including a conservative scenario that runs out of cash without further capital. Pods, the kitchen display, and a no-floor-staff service model are new to Utah inspectors and to guests. The Sensitivity section names each risk, and the Model integrity section lists every assumption with its source, date, and confidence.
body.purpose: Every company restaurant gives {givingPct} of its revenue to ONE RED STEP AT A TIME, a Utah mental health nonprofit. That is about {givingPerUnit} a year from one restaurant and {givingFiveYear} over the first five years. The pledge is a cost line in every scenario, so every margin in this plan already includes it.

kitchen.body: Every order lands on the kitchen display with a pod number. Broth, noodles, plating, in that order, on one wall.

corridor.body: Three staff corridors run forward from the kitchen like fingers. Pods line both sides, hatches facing in. A runner walks a corridor, not a dining room.

hatch.body: A sliding panel at the back of every pod. It opens to the corridor, the bowl goes through, it closes. The guest sees a bowl, not a hand.

journey.note: Real elapsed time {real}, shown in {anim} seconds. Kitchen time is compressed.

steps.paid: Paid at a lobby kiosk. About forty seconds on the screen, so the line keeps moving. No host.
steps.ticket: Ticket on the kitchen display: pod {pod}, corridor 2, west side.
steps.assigned: Pod {pod} assigned. The screen shows the way.
steps.broth: Broth station. A portion comes to temperature.
steps.walk: Across the cross-aisle, up guest aisle 2. Every door on the way is a pod. Not one is a kitchen.
steps.seated: Seated, facing the aisle. The hatch behind is closed. The room is quiet.
steps.noodles: Noodle station. Cooked to order, never held.
steps.plating: Plating. Smoked brisket sliced or rib chunks portioned to order, add-ons color coded to the ticket.
steps.corridor: A runner lifts the bowl and turns into staff corridor 2. Nobody in this corridor is a guest.
steps.delivered: Same pod, opposite sides. The guest never saw the corridor. The runner never stepped into an aisle. They did not share a square foot.
steps.finish: Finished. Out by the aisle, past the store, through the exit. No check, no tip.
steps.cleared: The runner clears by the corridor to the dish return. Same minute, different territory.
steps.exit: Out the exit. The two paths never crossed.
steps.reset: Pod {pod} wiped and reset. Six minutes, and the next number is on a screen.
steps.texted: The kiosk texts a live status link. The order is on the guest's phone before the walk begins.
steps.checkin: One tap on the phone: I'm at my pod. The kitchen knows the guest is seated.
steps.feed: The Live Kitchen Feed narrates the broth and noodles on the guest's phone, by name.
steps.fortune: A fortune cookie cracked while the noodles cook. The wait is shorter because it is full.
steps.addon: Extra noodles ordered from the phone. The kitchen sends them through the same hatch; nobody flags down a server.
steps.done: I'm done eating, tapped on the phone. The pod starts its reset before the guest reaches the aisle.

melbourne.name: Melbourne
melbourne.notes: Strong Asian dining culture, counter-seasonal to the Northern Hemisphere.

shanghai.name: Shanghai

kuala-lumpur.name: Kuala Lumpur
kuala-lumpur.notes: A large Chinese-Malaysian dining culture and English-language operations. A regional training kitchen for Southeast Asia.

bangkok.name: Bangkok
bangkok.notes: One of the world's great noodle cities, mall-driven dining, and a tourist base that already knows the format.

vancouver.name: Vancouver

beijing.name: Beijing

jakarta.name: Jakarta

manila.name: Manila

dubai.name: Dubai

mexico-city.name: Mexico City
mexico-city.notes: Latin America's first unit. A huge, food-serious city with a growing Asian dining scene.

geneva.name: Geneva

barcelona.name: Barcelona
barcelona.notes: Sub-franchise under the London agreement. Tourism volume and a young dining culture that adopts formats fast.

downsides.title: Named downsides, with what we do about them
downsides.subtitle: Each one is a lever move in the engine, not a paragraph. Steady-state EBITDA impact unless the card says otherwise: two are read in year one, one as payback, one on the consolidated year-five result.

slowRamp.title: Slow ramp
slowRamp.mitigation: Pre-opening kiosk demo and referral credits seeded in the corridor from the {launch} launch budget; a 15% weaker first year is inside the round-1 working capital reserve.

openingDelay.title: Opening slips a quarter
openingDelay.mitigation: Three dead months in front of the same curve, with the pre-opening payroll already running. The lease carries a rent abatement through the certificate of occupancy, and the flagship crew is hired against the inspection date, not the target date.

rentInflation.title: Rent inflation, +$15 per sq ft
rentInflation.mitigation: Ten-year terms with two options, TI allowance as a lever in every negotiation, and 3,500 sf footprints that keep occupancy a small share of revenue even at the higher rent.

beefSpike.title: Beef commodity spike, +5 points food cost
beefSpike.mitigation: Two grades on the menu, American Wagyu and USDA Prime, give the kitchen a lever when one of them moves; forward contracts through the commissary; and the give-aways are tier perks priced at cost, not blanket freebies, so a price move can be passed through without touching the program.

priceResistance.title: Price resistance, $2 off and 10% fewer covers
priceResistance.mitigation: The menu reset is the base case and the conservative case keeps today’s prices, so this is already the gap between them. The no-tip, all-in price is the argument; the kiosk lets us test price by daypart without reprinting anything.

copycat.title: A well-capitalized copycat, −20% utilization
copycat.mitigation: Oh! OS is the moat: pod orchestration, kiosk, kitchen display and delivery flow are ours. A copycat rents a room; it does not get the operating system.

memberProgramOverrun.title: Member program overrun, +1.5 points and +$20K swag
memberProgramOverrun.mitigation: The program is budgeted at {program} of revenue plus {swag} fixed, with ten paid referrals per member per month, a ninety-day expiry and perks priced at cost. Overrun is visible in the admin console weekly, and every perk has an off switch.

commissaryFailure.title: Commissary fails: broth drifts, +2 points food cost, 10% fewer covers
commissaryFailure.mitigation: Every batch is logged against the recipe so a drift shows up before a guest tastes it; each unit keeps a finishing kettle and a week of frozen base; St. George already runs its own kettle under the same recipe control.

podReliability.title: Pod hardware reliability
podReliability.mitigation: Five pods offline and higher maintenance modeled here. Spares at the commissary, a service SLA in the fabrication contract, and convertible duos that keep capacity when a partition fails.

accessibilityRedesign.title: Accessibility redesign, three pods lost
accessibilityRedesign.mitigation: Four accessible pods and a wider aisle are in the drawings today; this case assumes the plan review takes three more seats and adds buildout. The comb layout gives the seats back from the product store wall before it touches the kitchen.

laborShock.title: Utah labor or permitting shock
laborShock.mitigation: Wages up $3 and one extra FTE modeled. No front of house means the exposure is {people} people on a {hours}-hour day, not a dining room of servers. Permitting runs through the Utah County Health Department pathway already mapped in the roadmap.

capexOverrun.title: Build runs 15% over on pods, buildout and kitchen
capexOverrun.mitigation: Fixed-price pod fabrication after the prototype run, a TI allowance negotiated as a lever, and a contingency inside the round-1 working capital line. Read as payback, because that is what an overrun actually costs.

franchiseAttrition.title: A phase-one market stalls and royalties collect at 85%
franchiseAttrition.mitigation: Seattle stops after its first unit and royalties are collected at 85% across the system. Area-development agreements carry development schedules with a cure period, royalties are drawn by ACH on gross sales reported through Oh! OS, and the brand keeps the territory if the schedule is missed.

register.title: Disclosed, not modeled
register.subtitle: Risks a diligence reader will ask about that no lever captures. Each is stated with what we do about it; none is priced into the base case.

fireCodeAda.title: Fire code and ADA for pods
fireCodeAda.body: Seventy-five enclosed seats, egress through a corridor, and four accessible pods are drawn in; the fire marshal and the plan review decide the final count. The accessibility downside above prices three lost seats.

foodCode.title: Utah food code with no floor staff
foodCode.body: Service through a hatch with no server is reviewed under the Utah County Health Department pathway in the roadmap; a certified manager is on every shift and every runner holds a food handler permit.

techOutage.title: Kiosk, pod and kitchen-display outage
techOutage.body: Oh! OS runs on managed infrastructure with a paper fallback drilled at the flagship; a cellular backup carries payments and the kitchen display. A multi-hour outage on a peak day is a lost day, not a lost month.

beefSupply.title: Beef supply concentration
beefSupply.body: American Wagyu comes from a short list of ranches and USDA Prime brisket from a handful of packers. Two suppliers per grade, forward contracts through the commissary, and supplier quotes are an open item in the integrity section.

reviewBacklash.title: Review backlash and the launch concierge
reviewBacklash.body: A no-greeting room can read as cold in the first reviews. A floor concierge staffs the first ninety days at the flagship from the launch budget, and every review is answered by name.

cannibalization.title: Cannibalization between Utah units
cannibalization.body: Lehi, South Jordan and Provo sit within a forty-minute drive of each other. Trade areas are drawn at fifteen minutes; the engine does not net any overlap, so the Utah portfolio is modeled as five independent units.

keyPerson.title: Key person
keyPerson.body: The founder is the concept, the platform and the operator today. Key-person insurance is in overhead, the Director of Operations is hired before the second lease, and every process is written down in year one.

ip.title: IP and the assignment of Oh! OS
ip.body: The platform, the mark and the recipes are assigned to the LLC in the operating agreement; that agreement is still to be resolved and is listed as an open item. Franchisees license the software, they never own it.

dataPrivacy.title: Data privacy
dataPrivacy.body: Member data sits under the Utah Consumer Privacy Act today; London and Paris bring GDPR, mainland China brings PIPL with local hosting. Each international agreement carries its own data addendum and the cost is in the entry line for that structure.

pci.title: PCI scope
pci.body: Card data never touches Oh! OS: Stripe Terminal with point-to-point encryption at the kiosk and Stripe-hosted fields online. Scope is the SAQ a merchant of this size files, not a full assessment.

fx.title: Currency
fx.body: International royalties are earned in local currency and take a fixed haircut in the engine for conversion, withholding and timing. Rates are illustrative and dated; nothing is hedged.

exitMultiple.title: Exit multiple
exitMultiple.body: The restaurant multiple sits inside the small multi-unit range and the hybrid multiple only applies once recurring franchise profit is a real share of EBITDA. Neither is a promise; the Funding page lets a reader set their own.

sundayClosure.title: Closed Sundays
sundayClosure.body: A stated value, not a cost line. The engine runs on the operating days that result and every daily figure is scaled to them; the revenue given up is visible in the change log.

deliveryExcluded.title: Delivery excluded
deliveryExcluded.body: No third-party delivery is in the base case: the bowl is built for the pod, and the margin on a delivered bowl would not survive the commission. It stays an upside, not an assumption.

seasonality.title: Seasonality and dayparts
seasonality.body: The engine runs a flat utilization over the year. Utah has a January trough and a summer tourism lift that offset in the annual figure; a weak lunch daypart in a suburban unit is the single biggest local risk to it.

giftCardLiability.title: Gift-card and credit liability
giftCardLiability.body: Gift cards, member credits and referral credits are liabilities until redeemed. Breakage is not counted as revenue in the engine; unredeemed balances sit on the balance sheet and expire under the ninety-day rule where the law allows it.

cateringExcluded.title: Catering excluded from the base case
cateringExcluded.body: The catering channel was withdrawn from the customer site in September 2026 and remains an admin-only tool. Nothing from it is in the numbers; if it returns, it returns as its own line.

investorReporting.title: Investor reporting cadence
investorReporting.body: Monthly flash from Oh! OS by the tenth, a quarterly package with the consolidated table on the Financials page, and an audited year from year two. The overhead line already carries the audit.

relatedParty.title: Related party: the foundation
relatedParty.body: Oh! gives a fixed share of revenue to ONE RED STEP AT A TIME. Its founder is the owner's best friend, and the owner is its volunteer CTO with no compensation of any kind. No Oh! money flows to the owner through the foundation, and the pledge is fixed by a written agreement that investors can review.

experience.intro: Everyone in your party gets a pod, and every pod gets its own bowl. No host, no server, no check, no tip. Here is the whole visit, in order.

arrive.title: You walk in and nobody greets you.
arrive.body: That is the design. The room is quiet, the light is low, and the calligraphic mark on the far wall is the only thing asking for your attention. Three kiosks stand between you and seventy-five pods.
arrive.photo: The Oh! mark lit outside at dusk, reflected in the pool at the entrance

order.title: You order in about forty seconds.
order.body: Beef noodle soup is the menu. You choose your broth depth, your noodle, your add-ons, and your beef: smoked brisket slices or smoked beef rib chunks, in American Wagyu or USDA Prime. Add-ons are priced; members earn cashback and tier perks on every bowl. The kiosk already knows your name if you have been here before, and the moment you pay it texts you a live link to your order.
order.photo: Hands on the kiosk, add-on grid visible, the beef choice highlighted

walk.title: A pod number, and you go find it.
walk.body: Pod 32. You walk the aisle past a row of closed panels and the low murmur of a full room, every party in its own pods, side by side. Nobody is carrying a tray. Nobody is waiting to be seated.
walk.photo: The guest aisle looking down a row of numbered pods

settle.title: You sit, and the room disappears.
settle.body: Two and a third feet wide, four and a half deep. A hook for your bag, a shelf for your phone, water within reach. The panel in front of you is closed. One tap on your phone tells the kitchen you are in, and you can hear it, faintly, on the other side.
settle.photo: Inside a pod from the guest's seat, panel closed

status.title: Your phone runs the show.
status.body: The link opens a live page for your order, and it is written for you. While you wait, the Live Kitchen Feed narrates your bowl by name as it moves through the kitchen. Need anything? Tap it, and it comes through the same panel. No server required.
status.photo: The live order status page on a phone: Pod 32, the Live Kitchen Feed narrating the order, and the digital fortune cookie.
status.hint: This is the real status page, running a demo order. Tap anything; nothing reaches a real kitchen.

features.title: Live Kitchen Feed
features.body: AI narrates your order at every stage, by name, from the broth to the hatch.

features.title: A digital fortune cookie
features.body: A fortune written for you, lucky numbers, this day in history and a word of Chinese.

features.title: Order more to your pod
features.body: Refills, extra vegetables, a side or dessert, delivered through the hatch.

features.title: Call staff
features.body: One tap reaches the floor team. Nobody flags anyone down.

features.title: Roast My Order
features.body: Your choices, roasted. Your ingredients, given absurd life stories.

features.title: One Red Step
features.body: A mental health fact and a way to give, right where you already skipped the tip.

panel.title: The panel slides open.
panel.body: Seven minutes from the moment you paid, a bowl arrives through the wall. Your phone saw it coming. Broth first, then the smoked brisket or beef rib you chose, then the panel slides shut. You never see a hand.
panel.photo: The sliding panel mid-open, steam, the bowl arriving

taste.title: First spoon.
taste.body: Two-phase broth: a long bone simmer, then a finish built for flavor. Premium American beef, American Wagyu or Prime and nothing below it, smoked low and slow, then sliced as brisket or portioned as rib chunks. This is a premium fusion interpretation, and it does not pretend to be a grandmother's recipe. Want more? Extra noodles, a refill or a side are a tap away, and they come through the same panel.
taste.photo: Macro of the bowl: smoked brisket slices fanned, broth surface, noodles

leave.title: You finish, and you leave.
leave.body: One tap on your phone says you are done. No check. No tipping, because the people who made your bowl are salaried. If you are not a member yet, the page banks this order's points the moment you sign up, and if you brought someone, the referral credit lands when their first order completes. The pod resets behind you in under six minutes.

dtf.text: Din Tai Fung averages $27.4 million per US restaurant, the highest of any chain in the country and nearly twice the next (Technomic, via Restaurant Business, 2025). Braised beef noodle soup, a Taiwanese icon, is on its menu. It earns that with 300 to 400 people and about 10,000 square feet a room, roughly one worker per seat. We serve the same national dish from {pods} pods with {people} people. There is no Din Tai Fung in Utah.

tailwinds.title: Four things moving in our direction

asianFastCasual.title: Asian fast-casual is the fastest-growing segment
asianFastCasual.body: The category keeps taking share from both full-service and burger fast food, and beef noodle soup is under-represented in it relative to ramen and pho.

soloDining.title: Solo dining is normal now
soloDining.body: Counter seats and one-person tables are the fastest-growing reservation type. The pod is the honest version of that: privacy by design, not an apology.

laborCost.title: Labor cost pressure is pushing every operator toward automation
laborCost.body: We did not bolt a kiosk onto a dining room. We removed the dining room. Labor at {labor} of revenue, with {people} people running {pods} seats, is the result, and it is the line every restaurant operator will ask about first.

utahGrowth.title: Utah is the growth story lenders already know
utahGrowth.body: Fastest household formation in the country, a technology corridor with daytime density, and a proven record of concepts scaling out of the state.

market.references: Reference concepts: Ichiran proved the pod format at scale. Din Tai Fung proved Taiwanese food earns the highest unit volumes in America. Crumbl proved a Utah-founded concept can go national at speed, and every local lender and investor knows that story.

platform.title: The platform, in plain words
platform.body: Oh! OS is the software that runs the room: what the guest touches, what the kitchen sees, and what the owner reads. Four front doors, one API, one database, and two trusted services for money and identity.

guestPhone.title: The guest's phone does a server's job
guestPhone.body: The kiosk texts every guest a live link to their order. From the pod, one tap confirms they are seated, calls the floor team, or orders a refill, extra vegetables, a side or dessert, and each request lands on the kitchen display as its own ticket and comes back through the same hatch. Tapping "I'm done eating" starts the pod reset. The page also keeps the wait short and memorable: an AI kitchen feed that narrates the guest's own bowl by name, a digital fortune cookie, a roast of their order, and the One Red Step giving link. Nobody has to walk the aisles taking requests.

commissary.text: The flagship kitchen is built as the commissary from day one: a twelve-gallon steam-jacketed kettle line already production-tested, cook-chill for the long bone phase, and the flavor finish done on site in each unit. Utah units within sixty miles get the base broth by refrigerated van; St. George runs its own kettle under the same recipe control. Every batch is logged against the recipe so a drift shows up in data before a guest tastes it.

Rat.thingsToAvoid: Slow down on impulse decisions. The Horse year clashes with your energy, so ask extra questions before acting.

Ox.lookForwardTo: Your natural endurance shines while others burn out. Romance is strongly indicated. This is your year to find love!
Ox.thingsToAvoid: Don't resist change too strongly. Balance steady progress with warmth in relationships. Avoid overworking yourself.

Tiger.lookForwardTo: Momentum returns! Exciting opportunities in leadership and creative self-expression. Doors open with greater ease.
Tiger.thingsToAvoid: Don't neglect personal relationships while chasing achievements. Keep your loved ones close as you rise.

Rabbit.lookForwardTo: Your diplomacy and refined taste help you navigate situations smoothly without bulldozing through.
Rabbit.thingsToAvoid: Not everything will go as planned. Pick one brave decision and commit fully rather than trying to please everyone.

Dragon.lookForwardTo: The pace eases up, giving you breathing room for creativity and pleasure. Time to enjoy life's finer moments.
Dragon.thingsToAvoid: Prioritize experiences that refill you, not obligations that drain you. Stay flexible as situations unfold.

Snake.lookForwardTo: Competition sharpens you this year. Rising standards and capable peers force meaningful growth and leveling up.
Snake.thingsToAvoid: Put expectations in writing with collaborators. Focus on self-care and balance after an intense previous year.

Horse.lookForwardTo: Everything amplifies: your confidence, charm and magnetic appeal surge! You're the protagonist of 2026.
Horse.thingsToAvoid: This is your Ben Ming Nian (zodiac year). Wear red for luck! Protect finances from impulse spending and avoid major risks.

Goat.lookForwardTo: Doors open through people this year. Mentors, friends and collaborators bring unexpected blessings. It's a blossoming year!
Goat.thingsToAvoid: Stay generous with credit and follow through consistently. Don't spend too much time worrying about past or future.

Monkey.lookForwardTo: Your speed matches the year perfectly. Access to new opportunities multiplies. Relationships improve across the board.
Monkey.thingsToAvoid: Choose your best projects and finish them instead of chasing shiny distractions. Focus brings the biggest wins.

Rooster.lookForwardTo: Your precision and high standards become superpowers in this fast-paced year. Progress feels refreshing.
Rooster.thingsToAvoid: Swap critique for appreciation when possible. Embrace flexibility even when perfection isn't available.

Dog.lookForwardTo: Your reliability and follow-through finally get noticed and rewarded! You're among the luckiest signs in 2026.
Dog.thingsToAvoid: Accept care without picking it apart. Let your steadiness build trust over time rather than seeking instant validation.

Pig.lookForwardTo: Progress comes through consistency rather than dramatic pushes. Your endurance is perfectly suited for this year.
Pig.thingsToAvoid: Avoid forcing outcomes. Let impatient people burn themselves out while you stack steady progress.

hero.title: SMS opt-in consent
hero.lede: How Oh! Beef Noodle Soup asks for consent to send order texts, and how to stop them.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: We send transactional order texts only to customers who opt in. Consent is a clear checkbox that starts unchecked, and the customer must tick it. Consent is not required to make a purchase.

points.title: Key compliance points
items: The checkbox starts unchecked. Opting in takes an active tap.
Consent is separate from purchase. It is never required to complete an order.
The message types, frequency and data rates are disclosed.
The STOP and HELP keywords are shown.
A link to the privacy policy sits beside the consent.

language.title: Exact consent language
language.intro: This text appears next to the opt-in checkbox:
language.quote: I agree to receive SMS text messages from Oh Beef Noodle Soup regarding my order (confirmation & ready-for-pickup alerts). Message frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to unsubscribe.

types.title: Message types (transactional only)
types.intro: We only send texts about a customer's own order. We do not send marketing, promotional or advertising texts.

confirmation.label: Order confirmation
confirmation.body: Sent right after the order is placed, with the order number.

ready.label: Ready for pickup
ready.body: Sent when the order is ready at the restaurant.

frequency.label: Message frequency
frequency.body: 1 to 2 messages per order: one confirmation and one ready notice.

flow1.title: Opt-in flow 1: guest checkout
flow1.body: On the payment page, when a guest enters a phone number, an unchecked checkbox appears for SMS updates. It is not pre-checked: the customer must tap it to consent. The phone number is optional, and SMS consent is not required to complete the purchase.
flow1.alt: The SMS consent checkbox at guest checkout, unchecked by default
flow1.caption: Guest checkout payment page with the SMS consent checkbox, unchecked by default.

flow2.title: Opt-in flow 2: signed-in phone collection
flow2.body: Signed-in customers with no phone number on file see an optional prompt on the order confirmation page, after a successful payment, to add a number and consent to SMS updates. They can dismiss it with "Skip for now". A phone number is never required.
flow2.alt: The phone prompt for signed-in customers, with the SMS consent checkbox
flow2.caption: Phone prompt for signed-in customers, with the SMS consent checkbox unchecked by default.

meta.title: The experience: a visit to Oh!, step by step
meta.description: Arrive, order, walk, settle, taste, leave. A visit to Oh! Beef Noodle Soup in six steps, on the real floor plan. No host, no server, no check, no tip.

intro.title: A visit, in six steps.
intro.lede: Everyone in your party gets a pod, and every pod gets its own bowl. No host, no server, no check, no tip. Here is the whole visit, in order.

arrive.title: You walk in and nobody greets you.
arrive.body: That is the design. The room is quiet, the light is low, and three kiosks stand between you and the pods.

order.title: You order in about forty seconds.
order.body: Choose your broth depth, noodle, add-ons and beef: smoked brisket or beef rib, American Wagyu or USDA Prime. Pay, and the kiosk gives you a pod number and texts you a live link to your order.

walk.title: A pod number, and you go find it.
walk.body: You walk the aisle past a row of closed panels and the low murmur of a full room. Nobody is carrying a tray. Nobody is waiting to be seated.

settle.title: You sit, and the room disappears.
settle.body: A hook for your bag, a shelf for your phone, water within reach. One tap tells the kitchen you are in, and the Live Kitchen Feed narrates your bowl by name.

taste.title: First spoon.
taste.body: Minutes after you pay, your bowl arrives through the wall. You never see a hand. Want more? Extra noodles, a refill or a side come through the same panel.

leave.title: You finish, and you leave.
leave.body: One tap on your phone says you are done. No check, no tip line. Out past the store, and the pod resets behind you.
leave.alt: The store on the way out: shelves of sauces, gift boxes, bowls, shirts and caps, and a sign that says thank you.

map.note: City Creek, 75 pods. University Place is the same plan, mirrored, with 70.

comb.journeySummary: A visit on the floor plan. You walk from the entry to pod {label}, and your bowl comes down the staff corridor to your hatch.

order.a: At one of the kiosks in the lobby, in about forty seconds, or ahead on your phone. Either way, you get a pod number and a live link to your order.

together.a: Everyone in your party gets a pod, and every pod gets its own bowl. Duo pods are made for two: the partition between a pair comes out, and two pods become one.

server.a: No host and no server. Your bowl comes to the hatch of your pod from a staff corridor. Guests walk the aisles, staff walk the corridors, and the two meet only at the hatch.

more.q: What if I want more, or need help?
more.a: Tap it on your phone. Extra noodles, a refill, a side or dessert come through the same hatch, and one tap reaches the floor team.

phone.a: The link from your order opens a live page for it. The Live Kitchen Feed narrates your bowl as it moves through the kitchen, and one tap tells the kitchen you are in, and later that you are done.

tip.a: No. There is no check and no tip line. When you are done, one tap on your phone says so, and you leave when you are ready.

bowl.a: A two-phase broth, noodles and smoked American beef: brisket slices or beef rib chunks, in American Wagyu or USDA Prime. You choose the broth depth, the noodle and the add-ons.

members.a: Yes. Members earn 1% to 3% of every order back as credit toward their next orders, by tier, and a free bowl each time they move up a tier.
